# Aluminium PFC {#sec-aluminum}

`apps/aluminumNew` — a compact PFC application in the same family as
@sec-tungsten, parameterised for aluminium and built around a moving frame.

## Physical setting

The same phase-field crystal picture as @sec-tungsten: a conserved periodic
density whose minima are lattice sites. The differences are the equation of
state, an FCC seeding initial condition (`seed_grid_fcc`), and a moving-frame
formulation aimed at directional solidification, where the interesting physics
is a front travelling through the domain rather than a bulk relaxation.

## Governing equations

Conserved PFC dynamics, as in @eq-w-dyn:

$$
\partial_t \psi \;=\; \nabla^2 \frac{\delta F}{\delta \psi}.
$$

The free energy has the same structure as @eq-w-energy — a quadratic
correlation term plus a local polynomial in $\psi$ and the mean-field density
— with the aluminium coefficients $\bar p_2,\bar p_3,\bar p_4$ and
$\bar q_{20},\dots,\bar q_{40}$.

## Spectral formulation

$$
L(k) \;=\; u\,C(k), \qquad M_{\mathrm{nl}}(k) \;=\; u ,
\qquad u = k_{\mathrm{lap}} = -|\mathbf{k}|^2 .
$$ {#eq-al-symbol}

Alongside $C(k)$ the model carries a separate **correlation kernel** $P(k)$
applied to the density each step. The pointwise nonlinearity is therefore a
function of four arguments rather than two,

$$
N \;=\; N\big(\psi,\ \psi_{\mathrm{MF}},\ (P*\psi),\ T_{\mathrm{var}}(x,t)\big),
$$ {#eq-al-nl}

where $(P*\psi)$ is the kernel-filtered density — a convolution in real space,
hence a multiply in reciprocal space — and $T_{\mathrm{var}}$ is the imposed
temperature field.

## Moving frame and thermal drive

The temperature varies in space and time as a travelling profile,

$$
T_{\mathrm{var}}(x,t) \;=\;
  T_0 + G_{\mathrm{grid}}\big(x - x_{\mathrm{initial}} - V_{\mathrm{grid}}\,t\big),
$$ {#eq-al-temp}

clamped between `T_min` and `T_max`. A gradient $G_{\mathrm{grid}}$ pulled
through the domain at speed $V_{\mathrm{grid}}$ is the standard
directional-solidification setup: the front settles at the position where the
local temperature matches the interface condition, and then travels with the
gradient. Setting $G_{\mathrm{grid}}=0$ recovers an isothermal run at
`T_const`.

## Solution strategy

ETD1 as in @eq-etd1, dealiased, with the mean-field filter and the correlation
kernel evaluated as reciprocal-space multiplies. Two transforms per step plus
the kernel application.

## Verification

* **Regression.** Pinned checksums for the shipped case across CPU and GPU
  builds.
* **Schema.** JSON round-trip and range validation on every parameter.

Like @sec-tungsten this model has no closed-form reference; coverage is
regression and schema rather than analytical.

## Binaries and inputs

`aluminum_etd` (CPU), `aluminum_etd_cuda`, `aluminum_etd_hip`. Preset
`inputs_json/smoke.json`, plus `aluminumNew.json`.

## Scalability

Not measured. The application shares the spectral ETD stack with
@sec-tungsten, so its per-step cost is expected to track the tungsten curve at
equal grid size, but that has not been verified and no curve is reported here.
